newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gambling king and samba patron dies aged 71.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gambling king and samba patron dies aged 71.

text.p: Brazilian illegal gambling king Castor de Andrade, a colourful fixture of the annual Rio de Janeiro carnival, died of a heart attack on Friday at age 71, a hospital spokeswoman said.
De Andrade was the head of a network controlling the popular Brazilian "jogo do bicho", a type of gambling related to the lottery which resembles the numbers games of Harlem.
He was also a former president of the Bangu Atletico football club and financed the Mocidade Independente samba school, where his wake was held on Saturday.

De Andrade, known for his explosive temper, was serving a six-year sentence at the time of his death for forming an armed gang. Sentenced in 1993, he went into hiding for a year before being caught. In 1994 he was sentenced to another eight years for attempting to bribe a police chief. He was later allowed to serve his time at home because of cardiac problems.
De Andrade was also being investigated on accusations of murder, contraband and links to the drugs underworld. As head of Bangu Atletico, he was accused several times of bribing referees.

But newspapers fondly related tales of the eccentric businessman, including one occasion when he ran onto the field at Rio's hallowed Maracana stadium brandishing a gun after a referee awarded a penalty to opponents America. The referee then awarded a penalty to Bangu, who won the game 3-2.
Castor Goncalves de Andrade was born on Feb. 12, 1926, in Rio de Janeiro. He is survived by his second wife and four children.
